item.title: FBI arrests a woman accused of spying on Taiwan leader's family for China
item.description: The FBI and U.S. prosecutors say Wanying Zhang, also know as Heather, surveilled the Taiwanese president's son and his family.

item.title: Imran Khan supporters march in Pakistan to demand his release after talks failed
item.description: Talks between Khan's party and the government failed two days ago. Besides Khan's release, protesters demand his transfer to a hospital and family visits.

item.title: Nobel medicine prize goes to 3 scientists for research into brain activity
item.description: The Nobel Prize in medicine was awarded Monday to three scientists working on the mechanisms the brain uses to switch on, or off, the activity of individual nerve cells.

item.title: Former Prince Andrew files legal action to quash warrants that led to residence searches
item.description: A judicial spokesperson confirmed that Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor had filed a claim with the High Court in London and a hearing would take place Thursday.

item.title: Spain's prime minister calls early elections as pressure mounts over housing crisis
item.description: Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez announced early elections Monday after his government suffered a bruising legislative defeat last week on emergency measures related to the country's housing crisis.

item.title: Republicans and Democrats find a unifying target: Pharmacy benefit managers
item.description: Republicans and Democrats, both patients and politicians, seem united in their disdain for the healthcare companies known as pharmacy benefit managers. Tennessee and Arkansas are regulating them now.

item.title: From floating saunas to clinical trials: How heat might help mental health
item.description: While scientists have a decent understanding of how sauna and other forms of heat exposure exercises our cardiovascular system, they know relatively little about its impact on mental health.
